measures.title: An Act Restoring Political Party Primaries, Ending Ranked-Choice General Elections, and Repealing Recent Campaign Finance Laws
measures.shortSummary: Repeals Alaska's top-four open primary and ranked-choice general elections, restoring party primaries and single-choice general elections, and repeals 2020 campaign-finance disclosure rules.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the proposition (Alaska Const. art. XI §6); effective 90 days after certification.
measures.yesMeans: Yes: repeals top-four primaries and ranked-choice voting, restores party primaries and plurality general elections, and repeals 2020 campaign-finance rules.
measures.noMeans: Keeps top-four open primaries, ranked-choice general elections and the 2020 campaign-finance rules.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: An Act Addressing Voter Qualification
measures.shortSummary: Rewords Alaska voter-qualification law to state that only U.S. citizens who meet the other requirements may vote in any election; does not change existing requirements.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the proposition (Alaska Const. art. XI §6); effective 90 days after certification.
measures.yesMeans: Amends AS 15.05.010 to say 'Only a person who' is a U.S. citizen (and meets age, residency, registration rules) may vote at any election.
measures.noMeans: Current wording stays; citizenship is already required to vote.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to provide for the election of a Lieutenant Governor if the Office of Lieutenant Governor becomes vacant during the first two years of a term, to authorize the Legislature to set the salary of the Lieutenant Governor and officers of the Legislature, and to require any expenditure of legislative funds for travel to be approved by a legislative officer. Proposed by Act 2026-341.
measures.shortSummary: Requires an election to fill a Lieutenant Governor vacancy arising over 60 days before the next state general election; lets the Legislature set Lt. Governor and legislative officer pay by joint resolution; requires officer approval of legislative travel spending.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Ala. Const. 2022 §§284-285)
aliases: Elections for Lieutenant Governor Vacancies and Legislative Authority Over Salaries Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Alabama Constitution will be changed (vacancy election for Lt. Governor; Legislature sets Lt. Gov./officer pay by joint resolution; travel spending needs officer approval).
measures.noMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Alabama Constitution will not be changed; a Lt. Governor vacancy stays open until the next regular election and the Constitution keeps setting those salaries.

measures.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to require local boards of education to adopt policies requiring each public K-12 school to recite The Pledge of Allegiance to the United States flag at the beginning of each school day; and to require local boards of education to adopt a policy authorizing student-initiated and student-led prayer. Proposed by Act 2026-379.
measures.shortSummary: Requires local school boards to have each public K-12 school conduct the Pledge of Allegiance daily and to adopt policies allowing voluntary student-initiated, student-led prayer, with student opt-outs.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Ala. Const. 2022 §§284-285)
aliases: Require Pledge of Allegiance and Allow Student-Led Prayer in Public Schools Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Constitution will be changed to require daily Pledge policies and policies allowing student-led prayer.
measures.noMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Constitution will not be changed.

measures.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to provide a process for the creation of a consolidated county school system by merging two or more contiguous county boards of education; to require the State Board of Education to conduct an impact study...; to provide a procedure for protesting a proposed consolidation...; and to require the State Board of Education to adopt rules. Proposed by Act 2026-378.
measures.shortSummary: Lets two or more neighboring county school boards merge into one multi-county system by resolution, after a State Board of Education impact study; a 25% voter protest forces approval by voters in each affected county.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment statewide (Ala. Const. 2022 §§284-285)
measures.yesMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Constitution will be changed to create a county school-system merger process (impact study, protest procedure, State Board rules).
measures.noMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Constitution will not be changed; no constitutional process for merging county boards of education.

measures.title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of Alabama of 2022, to require local boards of education to adopt policies requiring each public K-12 school to broadcast or sanction the performance of the first stanza of The Star-Spangled Banner at least once per week during school hours. Proposed by Act 2026-424.
measures.shortSummary: Requires local school boards to have each public K-12 school broadcast, or allow a school-approved performance of, the first stanza of The Star-Spangled Banner at least once a week during school hours.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Ala. Const. 2022 §§284-285)
aliases: Broadcast The Star-Spangled Banner in Public Schools Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Constitution will be changed to require weekly national-anthem broadcast/performance policies.
measures.noMeans: Per Fair Ballot Commission: the Constitution will not be changed.

measures.title: A Constitutional Amendment to Be Known as "The Citizens Only Voting Amendment" and Providing That Only a Citizen of the United States Meeting the Qualifications of an Elector Under the Arkansas Constitution May Vote in an Election in this State.
measures.shortSummary: Amends Ark. Const. art. 3 §1 to state that only U.S. citizens meeting elector qualifications may vote in Arkansas elections, and that people not meeting them may not vote in any state or local election. Effective Jan 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment (Ark. Const. art. 19 §22)
measures.yesMeans: FOR: adds 'only a citizen of the United States' language to the Constitution's voter-qualification section; existing four qualifications unchanged.
measures.noMeans: AGAINST: Article 3 voter-qualification wording stays as is.

measures.title: A Constitutional Amendment to Amend Arkansas Constitution, Article 2, § 5, to Protect the Right to Keep and Bear Arms.
measures.shortSummary: Expands Ark. Const. art. 2 §5 to cover arms for lawful hunting, recreation and any lawful purpose, including ammunition, accessories and components, and declares the right natural, fundamental, individual and not to be infringed. Effective Jan 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment (Ark. Const. art. 19 §22)
aliases: Right to Keep and Bear Arms Amendment
measures.yesMeans: FOR: rewrites the arms section to add hunting/recreation/any lawful purpose, ammunition, accessories, components, and 'shall not be infringed' language.
measures.noMeans: AGAINST: existing art. 2 §5 language (common defense) remains.

measures.title: A Constitutional Amendment Concerning Economic Development in the State of Arkansas; and Authorizing the General Assembly to Provide for the Creation of Economic Development Districts Within Cities, Counties, or Cooperative Areas to Promote Economic Development Within the Economic Development District.
measures.shortSummary: Lets the legislature create economic development programs, loans and grants of public money and economic development districts that can issue bonds outside usual debt limits; district property taxed only by the district. Effective Jan 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment (Ark. Const. art. 19 §22)
aliases: Authorize Legislature to Create Programs for Economic Development Including Economic Development Districts Amendment
measures.yesMeans: FOR: authorizes economic development programs/loans/grants and districts with bonding and taxing powers; supersedes conflicting provisions.
measures.noMeans: AGAINST: no change to constitutional economic development provisions.

measures.title: Arkansas Water, Waste Disposal, and Pollution Abatement Facilities Financing Act of 2025.
measures.shortSummary: Authorizes the Arkansas Natural Resources Commission to issue up to $500 million in state general obligation bonds for water, waste disposal, pollution control, drainage, irrigation (max $165M), flood control and wetlands projects; max $60M per two years without legislative approval.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the question (Ark. Const. Amend. 20, state GO bonds)

measures.noMeans: AGAINST issuance of those bonds; the new bond authority is not granted.

measures.title: Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs. Legislative Statute.
measures.shortSummary: Authorizes $11.25 billion in state general obligation bonds for multifamily rental housing, veterans' home loans, supportive housing, preservation and downpayment assistance.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).
aliases: Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026

measures.title: Increases State's Rainy Day Fund. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.
measures.shortSummary: Raises the cap on the state's Budget Stabilization Account (rainy day fund) and changes reserve and extra debt-payment rules, including treatment under the state spending limit.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).
measures.yesMeans: Rules for building state budget reserves and paying down extra state debts would change; reserves would be higher and extra debt payments required for longer.
measures.noMeans: Rules for building state budget reserves and paying down extra state debts would not change.

measures.title: Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
measures.shortSummary: Makes permanent the 2012 voter-approved income tax rates on high earners (currently set to expire in 2031) and allocates the revenue to public education.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Healthcare by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes

measures.noMeans: An income tax increase on high-income earners in place since 2012 would expire in 2031.

measures.title: Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes. Initiative Statute.

measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.shortSummary: Authorizes $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds for immunology and immunotherapy research, half to one UC-affiliated nonprofit institute and half to research grants.

measures.title: Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
measures.shortSummary: Requires government ID to vote in person and last four digits of a government ID number on mail-ballot envelopes; free state voter ID card; officials must verify and report voter citizenship.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.yesMeans: Voters would be required to present additional identifying information to elections officials each time they vote.
measures.noMeans: A voter's identity would continue to be established with the voter's signature.

measures.title: Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns. Legislative Statute.
measures.shortSummary: Repeals the ban on state and local public financing of candidate campaigns; public programs could not use funds earmarked for education, transportation or public safety.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.title: Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers. Initiative Constitutional Amendment and Statute.
measures.shortSummary: Imposes a one-time 5% tax on net worth of California taxpayers and trusts with assets over $1 billion; revenue mainly for health care, also food assistance/education; exempt from school-funding and spending-limit rules.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.title: Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
measures.shortSummary: Nullifies state taxes enacted after Jan 1, 2026 whose revenue is exempted from the voter-approved spending limit, and requires State Auditor reviews of programs funded by new special taxes.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.noMeans: The State Auditor's review duties and the state spending limit requirements would not change.

measures.title: Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes. Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
measures.shortSummary: Bars new state taxes on ownership of personal property (anything other than real estate) or that apply retroactively; nullifies conflicting taxes enacted after Jan 1, 2026.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).
aliases: Retirement and Personal Savings Protection Act of 2026
measures.yesMeans: The state could not establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
measures.noMeans: The state would continue to have the option to establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.

measures.title: Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services. Legislative Constitutional Amendment.
measures.shortSummary: From Jan 1, 2027, requires two-thirds voter approval for local special taxes proposed by citizen initiative (now majority) and bars local initiatives imposing ad valorem property taxes.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

two-thirds vote for local special taxes

measures.title: Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% of Revenue on Program Services. Initiative Statute.
measures.shortSummary: Penalizes nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers that spend less than 90% of revenue on program services advancing their charitable purpose, including patient care.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.noMeans: The new requirement on health care clinic spending would not go into effect.

measures.title: Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects. Initiative Statute.
measures.shortSummary: Amends CEQA to speed environmental review for many housing, transportation, water, health and energy projects, with deadlines for review and for resolving lawsuits.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).
measures.yesMeans: Certain projects would get new review and court-challenge procedures, with tighter time limits and narrower court review.
measures.noMeans: Projects would continue to use existing review and court-challenge procedures.

measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Cal. Const. art. II §10(a); art. XVIII §4 for amendments). If conflicting measures both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails (art. II §10(b)).

measures.noMeans: Voters would continue to be asked who should fill the vacancy as part of recall elections.

measures.noMeans: No constitutional notification requirement; current state limits on cooperation continue.

measures.title: Right to Natural Gas
measures.shortSummary: Creates a constitutional right for consumers to buy natural gas for cooking or heating in homes and businesses, and for distributors and utilities to sell it.
measures.approvalRule: 55% of votes cast on the measure (Colo. Const. art. V §1(4)(b)); SOS: 'Requires 55% approval because it adds language to the state constitution'
measures.yesMeans: Adds a constitutional right to purchase and sell natural gas for cooking/heating.
measures.noMeans: No such constitutional right; natural gas use remains governed by statute and regulation.

measures.title: Constitutional Right to Hunt and Fish
measures.shortSummary: Creates a constitutional right to hunt and fish by traditional methods and makes hunting and fishing the preferred means of managing wildlife, while preserving state regulation for science and safety.
measures.approvalRule: 55% of votes cast on the measure (Colo. Const. art. V §1(4)(b)); SOS: 'Requires 55% approval because it adds language to the state constitution'; Blue Book: 'Passes with 55 percent of the vote'
measures.yesMeans: Establishes a state constitutional right to hunt and fish (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Hunting and fishing continue as allowed under existing state and federal law (Blue Book).

measures.title: Mail Ballot Voter Identification
measures.shortSummary: Requires mail voters in federal and state elections to add the last four digits of their SSN or Colorado ID/driver's license number to the ballot envelope, with a cure process; uncured ballots are not counted.
measures.approvalRule: 55% of votes cast on the measure (Colo. Const. art. V §1(4)(b)); SOS: 'Requires 55% approval because it adds language to the state constitution'; Blue Book: 'Passes with 55 percent of the vote'
measures.yesMeans: Voters must provide ID information with their mail ballot in addition to a signature (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Continues the current signature-only verification for mail ballots (Blue Book).

measures.title: Plain Language Ballot Questions
measures.shortSummary: Requires state and local ballot questions to be in plain language at no more than an 8th-grade reading level and bars statutes requiring conflicting language in citizen-initiative ballot titles.
measures.approvalRule: 55% of votes cast on the measure (Colo. Const. art. V §1(4)(b)); SOS: 'Requires 55% approval because it adds language to the state constitution'; Blue Book: 'Passes with 55 percent of the vote'
measures.yesMeans: Ballot titles must be plain language at an eighth-grade level; laws may not interfere (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Keeps current plain-language requirement without a specific reading-level standard (Blue Book).

measures.title: Congressional Redistricting
measures.shortSummary: Puts the current congressional redistricting process in the constitution and bars off-cycle map changes unless approved by the independent commission and Colorado Supreme Court after public meetings and without partisan favoritism.
measures.approvalRule: 55% of votes cast on the measure (Colo. Const. art. V §1(4)(b)); SOS: 'Requires 55% approval because it adds language to the state constitution'; Blue Book: 'Passes with 55 percent of the vote'
measures.yesMeans: Commission (and Supreme Court) must approve any congressional map change outside a scheduled redistricting year (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Continues the current every-ten-years congressional redistricting requirements (Blue Book).

measures.title: Graduated Income Tax
measures.shortSummary: Replaces Colorado's flat 4.4% income tax with graduated rates (3.7%-8.4%) from 2027, raising about $2.7 billion yearly for K-12, health care and child care, exempt from the TABOR limit.

measures.yesMeans: Creates a graduated income tax; extra revenue goes to K-12, health care and early childhood, exempt from the revenue limit (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Keeps the constitutional requirement for a flat state income tax rate (Blue Book).

measures.title: Penalties for Fentanyl Crimes
measures.shortSummary: Raises felony classifications for fentanyl and similar synthetic opioid possession and distribution, mandates treatment for some offenses, and narrows sentencing exemptions, including for drug-related deaths.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (statutory; SOS/Blue Book: 'Passes with a majority vote')
measures.yesMeans: Possession of any amount of fentanyl becomes a felony; 8-year mandatory minimum for distribution; fewer penalty reductions (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Minor fentanyl possession stays a misdemeanor and tiered felony penalties remain (Blue Book).

measures.title: Penalties for Human Trafficking of a Minor
measures.shortSummary: Makes child sex trafficking punishable by mandatory life in prison without parole and expands the crime to include buying sexual activity with a minor.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (statutory; SOS/Blue Book: 'Passes with a majority vote')
measures.yesMeans: Life without parole for child sex trafficking; crime expanded to buying sex with a minor (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Keeps current felony penalties (8-48 years plus mandatory parole) (Blue Book).

measures.title: Male and Female Participation in School Sports
measures.shortSummary: Requires K-12 and college sports teams to be designated male, female or coed and limits participation to the team matching a student's biological sex, with an exception for females on male teams.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (statutory; SOS/Blue Book: 'Passes with a majority vote')
aliases: Male and Female Participation in School and Collegiate Sports
measures.yesMeans: School teams designated by biological sex or as mixed; schools must adopt sex-eligibility policies (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Schools and athletic associations keep setting their own eligibility policies under current law (Blue Book).

measures.title: Prohibit Certain Surgeries on Minors
measures.shortSummary: Prohibits surgery on minors to alter biological sex characteristics in response to a minor's perception of sex or gender, and bars public funds or insurance from paying for it.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (statutory; SOS/Blue Book: 'Passes with a majority vote')
aliases: Prohibit Surgery on Minors in Response to Perception of Sex or Gender
measures.yesMeans: Bans these surgeries on minors and bars government funds or insurance from paying (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Keeps current law protecting access and allowing insurance coverage (Blue Book).

measures.title: Income Tax Rate Cap
measures.shortSummary: Caps the state income tax rate for individuals and corporations at 4.4% of federal taxable income in statute, starting January 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (statutory; SOS/Blue Book: 'Passes with a majority vote')
measures.yesMeans: Sets the current 4.4% rate as the statutory maximum (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Keeps the 4.4% rate without a new statutory limit (Blue Book).

measures.title: Designate Sporting Goods Sales Tax Revenue for Conservation
measures.shortSummary: Directs part of existing state sales tax on sporting goods to conservation, wildfire prevention and outdoor recreation programs as a voter-approved revenue change exempt from the TABOR limit.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (statutory; SOS/Blue Book: 'Passes with a majority vote')
aliases: Direct Sporting Goods Sales Tax Revenue for Conservation
measures.yesMeans: Sporting-goods sales tax revenue funds conservation/wildfire/recreation programs, exempt from revenue limits (Blue Book).
measures.noMeans: Revenue stays in the general budget subject to the revenue limit (Blue Book).

measures.title: State Public K-12 Education Funding
measures.shortSummary: Raises state K-12 investment 2% a year for ten years, funded by raising the TABOR spending limit by the amount spent on K-12 as a voter-approved revenue change, with annual independent audits.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast (SOS: 'Passes with a majority vote. Referred to the voters by state legislature.')
measures.yesMeans: State may keep revenue above the TABOR limit to increase K-12 spending 2%/yr for 10 years (per ballot question).
measures.noMeans: No change to the spending limit for this purpose; above-cap revenue continues to be refunded.

measures.title: Exemption of Tangible Personal Property on Agricultural Land from Taxation
measures.shortSummary: Exempts from property tax tangible personal property habitually located on agriculturally classified land, used for agricultural production or agritourism, and owned by the landowner or leaseholder, starting with tax year 2027.
measures.approvalRule: 60% of votes cast on the measure (Fla. Const. art. XI §5(e))
aliases: Exempt Tangible Personal Property Used for Agriculture or Agritourism from Property Taxes Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Qualifying farm/agritourism tangible personal property on agricultural land becomes exempt from ad valorem tax, first applying to tax years beginning Jan 1, 2027.
measures.noMeans: Such property remains subject to ad valorem tax as under current law.

measures.title: Increased Homestead Exemption; Lower Cap on Increases in Non-Homestead Property Assessments
measures.shortSummary: Raises the non-school homestead exemption to $150,000 (2027) and $250,000 (2028, then inflation-indexed), cuts the non-homestead assessment-increase cap from 10% to 5%, phases in for new residents, and limits local property-tax spending purposes.
measures.approvalRule: 60% of votes cast on the measure (Fla. Const. art. XI §5(e))
aliases: Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes
Homestead Tax Exemptions, Property Assessments, and Spending Restrictions Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Non-school homestead exemption $150k in 2027, $250k in 2028 (CPI-indexed after); local options to go higher; non-homestead cap 10%→5%; local property taxes limited to listed core purposes; effective Jan 1, 2027.
measures.noMeans: Current homestead exemptions, 10% non-homestead assessment cap and local levy purposes remain unchanged.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: Budget Stabilization Fund
measures.shortSummary: Raises the cap on Florida's budget stabilization (rainy-day) fund from 10% to 25% of general revenue collections, requires annual transfers of up to $750 million absent certain conditions, and allows withdrawals for critical state needs.
measures.approvalRule: 60% of votes cast on the measure (Fla. Const. art. XI §5(e): 'approved by vote of at least sixty percent of the electors voting on the measure')
aliases: Changes to Budget Stabilization Fund Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Fund cap rises from 10% to 25% of general revenue; Legislature must transfer the lesser of $750M or the amount needed to reach 25% each year unless conditions are met; withdrawals allowed for critical state needs.
measures.noMeans: Current 10% cap and existing fund rules stay in place.

measures.title: Increases the maximum qualifying acreage for assessment and taxation as bona fide conservation use property.
measures.shortSummary: Doubles the maximum acreage a single owner may enroll as bona fide conservation use (preferentially assessed agricultural and timber) property, from 2,000 to 4,000 acres.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Ga. Const. art. X, §I, ¶II: 'ratified by a majority of the electors qualified to vote for members of the General Assembly voting thereon')
aliases: Increase Acre Limit for Agriculture and Timber Conservation Use Property Tax Classification Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Up to 4,000 acres of a single owner's farm/timber land may qualify for conservation use assessment.
measures.noMeans: The 2,000-acre limit stays.

measures.title: Authorizes creation of Georgia Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund for 9-1-1 systems expansion, maintenance, and operation.
measures.shortSummary: Lets the General Assembly create a Georgia Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund and dedicate certain existing revenues to it; money could be used only for expanding, maintaining and operating 9-1-1 systems.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Ga. Const. art. X, §I, ¶II)
aliases: Authorize Creation of Next Generation 9-1-1 Fund Amendment
measures.yesMeans: General Assembly may dedicate certain existing revenues to a nonlapsing fund used only for 9-1-1 systems.
measures.noMeans: No constitutional authorization for a dedicated 9-1-1 fund.

measures.title: Provides for the nonpartisan election of all probate court judges.
measures.shortSummary: Requires that all Georgia probate court judges be elected in nonpartisan elections.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Ga. Const. art. X, §I, ¶II)
aliases: Require Nonpartisan Elections for Probate Judges Amendment
measures.yesMeans: All probate judges would be elected on a nonpartisan basis.
measures.noMeans: Probate judge elections continue as now (generally partisan).

measures.title: Increasing the Timeframe for the Hawaii Senate to Consider and Act on Judicial Appointments.
measures.shortSummary: Gives the state Senate 60 days instead of 30 to act on judicial appointments made between April 1 and December 31 when it is not in regular session or is about to adjourn.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes tallied on the question AND yes votes ≥50% of all ballots cast at the election (Haw. Const. art. XVII §3; blank/over votes effectively count against). Turnout-style rule: yes votes must be at least 50% of total ballots cast in the general election, not just of votes on the question.
measures.yesMeans: Senate gets 60 days (up from 30) to consider and act on judicial appointments made April 1–December 31 outside/at end of regular session.
measures.noMeans: The Senate's 30-day window to act on those judicial appointments stays.

measures.title: Directing the Hawaii State Legislature to Establish Procedures for Counties to Issue RISE Bonds, Exempt from County Debt Limits.
measures.shortSummary: Directs the legislature to let counties issue 'resilient infrastructure for shelter and equity' (RISE) bonds for district improvements, repaid from property-tax growth, excluded from county debt limits.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes tallied on the question AND yes votes ≥50% of all ballots cast at the election (Haw. Const. art. XVII §3; blank/over votes effectively count against). Turnout-style rule: yes votes must be at least 50% of total ballots cast in the general election, not just of votes on the question.
aliases: Resilient Infrastructure for Shelter and Equity bonds
measures.yesMeans: Legislature must authorize counties to issue RISE bonds repaid solely from property-tax growth in designated districts, outside county debt limits.
measures.noMeans: No constitutional authorization for RISE bonds outside county debt limits.

measures.title: Shall the following amendment to the Constitution be adopted? (new Article XIII: two-thirds vote of each house required to raise income tax rates or create a new income tax)
measures.shortSummary: Requires a two-thirds vote of all members of each legislative chamber to raise individual or corporate income tax rates or create any new state income tax; local-option taxes excluded; one-year limit on enactment challenges.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the amendment (Iowa Const. art. X, sec. 1)
aliases: Two-Thirds Legislative Vote Requirement for Income Tax Increase Bills Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Adds new Article XIII: bills raising income-type tax rates or creating a new tax on income or legal and special reserves need 2/3 of members elected to each house.
measures.noMeans: Constitution unchanged; such tax bills keep needing a simple majority.

measures.title: Amendment to Idaho Constitution - House Joint Resolution 4 (Section 26, Article III, psychoactive substances)
measures.shortSummary: Gives only the Idaho Legislature power to legalize marijuana, narcotics or other psychoactive substances, removing the citizen initiative route for drug legalization.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (Idaho Const. art. XX §1, 'majority of the electors')
aliases: legislature exclusive authority to legalize drugs
measures.yesMeans: Legislature gets exclusive authority to legalize marijuana, narcotics or psychoactive substances (pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: No change; controlled-substance laws can still be changed by initiative (pamphlet).

measures.title: Amendment to Idaho Constitution - House Joint Resolution 6 (new Section 8, Article X, English official language)
measures.shortSummary: Makes English the official language of Idaho in the constitution and requires English in public proceedings, documents, instruction and acts, except as federal law requires.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (Idaho Const. art. XX §1, 'majority of the electors')
measures.yesMeans: Designates English the official state language in the constitution (pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: No constitutional change; English remains official language in statute only (pamphlet).

measures.title: Proposition One: Reproductive Freedom & Privacy Act
measures.shortSummary: Initiated statute creating a right to abortion before fetal viability and afterward in medical emergencies, a reproductive privacy right, and liability protections for providers; effective Jan 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (initiated statute)
measures.yesMeans: Creates a right to abortion before viability and post-viability in medical emergencies; provider protections; statutory reproductive privacy right (pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: Keeps current law banning abortion except to prevent death and early-pregnancy reported rape/incest (pamphlet).

measures.title: Which of the following guns should be designated as the state gun of Idaho? Please choose only one answer.
measures.shortSummary: Non-binding question asking voters to pick one of six firearms as Idaho's official state gun; the Legislature must act later to make a designation.
measures.approvalRule: None; non-binding advisory question. Pamphlet sets no approval threshold; result informs a future legislative designation.
measures.yesMeans: Not a yes/no question: voters choose one of (a) Winchester 1894, (b) Winchester 1873, (c) 1873 Colt SAA 'Peacemaker', (d) M1 Garand, (e) Colt M1911, (f) Remington 700.
measures.noMeans: Not applicable (multiple-choice, non-binding).
measures.marketNote: This is an advisory question with multiple choices, rather than a Pass/Fail vote. No linked market yet.

measures.title: Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to provide that a person charged with an offense other than murder or treason is not entitled to bail if: (1) the proof is evident or the presumption strong; and (2) the state proves by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect the safety of any other person or the community? (Article 1, Section 17)
measures.shortSummary: Lets courts deny bail to people charged with offenses other than murder or treason when proof is evident and the state shows by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions can protect others or the community.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the public question (Ind. Const. art. 16, sec. 1)
aliases: Bailable Offenses and Substantial Risk Standard Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Amends Art. 1 sec. 17 to allow denial of bail for any offense when the proof standard and clear-and-convincing public-safety showing are met.
measures.noMeans: Only murder and treason remain non-bailable when proof is evident or presumption strong.

measures.title: Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to permit the judge of a city or town court to reside in: (1) the county in which the court is located; or (2) the bordering county closest to the city or town in which the court is located? (Article 6, Section 6)
measures.shortSummary: Lets city and town court judges live in the county where the court sits or the bordering county closest to the city or town, rather than within the city or town itself.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the public question (Ind. Const. art. 16, sec. 1)
aliases: city and town court judges residency
Residency Requirements for City and Town Court Judges Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Amends Art. 6 sec. 6 to allow these judges to reside in the court's county or the closest bordering county.
measures.noMeans: Current residency requirement for city and town court judges stays.

measures.title: Explanatory statement: This amendment would clarify only a person who is a citizen of the United States is eligible to vote in this state.
measures.shortSummary: Amends Art. 5 sec. 1 to state that no person is a qualified elector unless a U.S. citizen, at least 18, and (unless an exception applies) a resident of the voting area.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the amendment (Kan. Const. art. 14, sec. 1)
measures.yesMeans: A vote for this proposition would clarify that only a person who is a citizen of the United States is eligible to vote in this state.
measures.noMeans: A vote against this proposition would make no change to the constitution of the state of Kansas, and the language concerning voter qualifications would remain the same.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: AN ACT proposing to amend Section 77 of the Constitution of Kentucky relating to limiting the Governor's ability to grant pardons and commute sentences.
measures.shortSummary: Bars the Governor from granting pardons, reprieves or commutations from 60 days before a gubernatorial election until the fifth Tuesday after it (new term begins); makes Section 77 gender-neutral.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast for and against the amendment (Ky. Const. §256)
aliases: Limit Governor's Pardon Power and Commutations Near General Election Amendment
measures.yesMeans: YES to: 'Are you in favor of limiting a Governor's ability to grant pardons or commute sentences by prohibiting him or her from granting pardons or commuting sentences during the time period beginning 60 days prior to the general election at which the Governor is elected, and ending when the Governor is sworn in...' (Section 77 amended).
measures.noMeans: NO: Section 77 unchanged; no pre-election/transition blackout on pardons or commutations.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to increase the maximum amount of income a person may receive and still qualify for the special assessment level for residential property receiving the homestead exemption? (Effective January 1, 2027) (Amends Article VII, Section 18(G)(1)(a)(ii))
measures.shortSummary: Raises the adjusted-gross-income cap for the special assessment level (homestead assessment freeze for seniors 65+, disabled veterans and others) from $100,000 to $150,000, CPI-indexed from 2028; lets assessors verify income via state tax returns.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Raise Income Limit to $150,000 for Special Property Tax Assessment Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Income cap for the special assessment level rises from $100,000 to $150,000 AGI (indexed from 2028); effective 2027.
measures.noMeans: Cap stays at $100,000 AGI, inflation-indexed from 2026.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to prohibit expropriation of property by a foreign adversary or an agent of a foreign adversary? (Amends Article I, Section 4(B)(4))
measures.shortSummary: Bars any private entity that is a foreign adversary or an agent of a foreign adversary, as defined by law, from expropriating (taking or damaging) property through eminent domain.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Prohibit Property Expropriation by Foreign Adversaries Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Foreign adversaries or their agents (as defined by law) may not use expropriation to take or damage property.
measures.noMeans: Existing private-entity expropriation rules remain, with no foreign-adversary ban in the constitution.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to prohibit a person who has served more than one and one-half terms as governor from being elected as governor for any future term? (Amends Article IV, Section 3(B))
measures.shortSummary: Replaces the limit on serving more than one and one-half terms in two consecutive terms with a lifetime limit: anyone who has served more than one and one-half terms as governor could not be elected governor again.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
measures.yesMeans: Lifetime limit: a person who has served more than 1.5 terms as governor can never again be elected governor.
measures.noMeans: Current consecutive-term limit stays; a two-term governor may run again after sitting out a term.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to allow a local taxing authority to continue to levy a lower millage rate without losing its ability to adjust to the maximum authorized millage rate from a prior year's reassessment? (Effective January 1, 2027) (Amends Article VII, Section 23(C))
measures.shortSummary: Lets a local taxing authority that levies below its maximum authorized millage keep the ability to later raise it, by two-thirds board vote after a public hearing, up to the maximum from a prior reassessment, instead of losing that ability.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Property Tax Rate Limits Based on Existing Voter-Approved Maximums Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Taxing authorities that levy below the maximum keep the right to later raise millage to a prior reassessment's maximum (2/3 board vote plus hearing, no new voter approval), from 2027.
measures.noMeans: Current rule stays: an authority that does not roll forward before the next reassessment permanently loses that headroom.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to prohibit a defendant from being released on any post-conviction bail if the defendant is convicted of an aggravated offense against a minor child? (Adds Article I, Section 18(C))
measures.shortSummary: Bars any post-conviction bail for a person convicted of an 'aggravated offense' as defined in R.S. 15:541 (a list of serious sex offenses such as first- or second-degree rape) committed against a victim who is a minor.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Prohibit Post-Conviction Bail for Individuals Convicted of Assault Against Minors Amendment
no bail after conviction for child sex offenses
measures.yesMeans: People convicted of an aggravated offense (R.S. 15:541) against a minor cannot be released on post-conviction bail.
measures.noMeans: Post-conviction bail for these offenders remains governed by existing law.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to allow property tax exemptions for blighted or derelict properties that have been rehabilitated, and to require the legislature to enact laws providing for administration of these exemptions? (Effective January 1, 2027) (Adds Article VII, Section 21(P))
measures.shortSummary: Creates an optional property tax exemption for blighted or derelict property that has been rehabilitated; the legislature must define terms and set the exemption's term, conditions and procedures for local administration. Effective 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Tax Exemption for Rehabilitated Property Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Allows an optional property tax exemption for rehabilitated blighted/derelict property, under terms the legislature sets by law.
measures.noMeans: No such exemption is added to the constitution's exclusive list of exemptions.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to authorize a state retirement system to apply any nonrecurring state monies it receives to any of its unfunded accrued liability rather than requiring application to its oldest unfunded accrued liability? (Amends Article VII, Section 10(D)(2)(b)(iii))
measures.shortSummary: Removes the requirement that state retirement systems apply the constitutionally required share (at least 25%) of nonrecurring state money to their oldest unfunded accrued liability first, letting them apply it to any of their UAL.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Remove Payment Order Requirement for State Retirement System Unfunded Liability Amendment
Removing Payment Order Requirement for State Retirement System Unfunded Liability Amendment
measures.yesMeans: State retirement systems may apply nonrecurring state money to any part of their unfunded accrued liability.
measures.noMeans: Systems must keep applying such money to their oldest amortization bases first.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to authorize parishes and municipalities to extend an additional property tax exemption for property subject to the homestead exemption that is owned and occupied by a person who is at least sixty-five years of age and who qualifies for the special assessment level? (Effective January 1, 2028) (Adds Article VII, Section 21(P))
measures.shortSummary: Authorizes an extra homestead exemption for owners 65+ who qualify for the special assessment level, rising with age from $6,000 to $30,000 of assessed value; applies only where local voters approve it. Effective 2028.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)). Separately, the exemption applies in a parish/municipality only after a later local majority vote (new §21(P)(3)); that is implementation, not ratification.
aliases: Property Tax Exemption for Seniors Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Parishes/municipalities may, after local voter approval, grant seniors 65+ on the special assessment level an added exemption of $6,000-$30,000 assessed value (by age), from 2028.
measures.noMeans: No new senior exemption; existing homestead exemption and special assessment freeze remain.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to allow the surviving spouse of a deceased veteran with a service-connected disability, who receives the additional property tax exemption, to make a one-time transfer of the additional property tax exemption to a subsequent qualifying property? (Effective January 1, 2027) (Amends Article VII, Section 21(K)(1))
measures.shortSummary: Lets the surviving spouse of a service-disabled veteran who receives the additional homestead property tax exemption transfer it once to a new homestead, capped at the amount claimed on the prior homestead. Effective Jan. 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: One-Time Transfer of Disabled Veteran Homestead Tax Exemption for Surviving Spouses Amendment
disabled veteran surviving spouse property tax exemption
measures.yesMeans: A surviving spouse of a disabled veteran may make a one-time transfer of the additional homestead exemption to a new qualifying homestead (capped at the prior amount), from 2027.
measures.noMeans: No transfer right; the surviving-spouse exemption stays tied to the original property.

measures.title: Do you support an amendment to allow for the use of public funds by a political subdivision for the purpose of identifying, inventorying, removing or replacing drinking water utility service lines made of or affected by materials as specified or prescribed by the Lead and Copper Rule Improvements of the United States Environmental Protection Agency, promulgated October 30, 2024, or subsequent promulgation, on property owned by utility customers? (Amends Article VII, Section 14)
measures.shortSummary: Adds an exception to the constitutional ban on donating public funds so political subdivisions may pay to identify, inventory, remove or replace drinking-water service lines covered by EPA's Lead and Copper Rule Improvements on customers' property.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of electors voting on the amendment statewide (La. Const. art. XIII §1(C)); no local-majority requirement.
aliases: Use Public Funds for Drinking Water Utility Service Lines Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Local governments may spend public funds on lead/regulated service-line inventory, removal and replacement on customer-owned property.
measures.noMeans: The ban on donating public funds continues to bar such spending on private property.

measures.shortSummary: Makes most records of the Legislature and the Governor's office subject to the Public Records Law, exempting policy-development materials and certain constituent communications.

measures.shortSummary: Specifies that employees of the Committee for Public Counsel Services (the state public defender agency) may form a union and bargain collectively with their employer.

measures.title: State Primary Elections
measures.shortSummary: Replaces separate party primaries for state offices with one primary listing all candidates on a single ballot; voters may choose any candidate and the top two vote-getters advance to the general election.

measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would make no change to the laws governing primary elections.

measures.title: Election Day Registration
measures.shortSummary: Lets eligible citizens register to vote, or update their registration address, at their polling place on Election Day.

measures.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would permit eligible citizens to register to vote or to update their voter registration address at their polling place on Election Day.
measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would make no change to the laws governing voter registration.

measures.title: State Revenue Limit & Rebate
measures.shortSummary: Changes the state tax-revenue cap (Chapter 62F), tying it to prior-year collections plus average wage and salary growth, and requires rebating revenue above the limit.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question AND yes votes >= 30% of total ballots cast at the state election (Mass.
