aliases: Initiative Petition for a Law Relative to Limiting State Tax Collection Growth and Returning Surpluses to Taxpayers
measures.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would change the limit on state revenue collection, tying it to prior year collections plus average wage and salary growth, and provide for a rebate of revenue exceeding that limit.
measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would make no change in the law relative to state revenue collection.

measures.title: Natural Resource Conservation Fund
measures.shortSummary: Creates the Nature for All Fund for natural-resource conservation, funded by a share of existing state sales and use taxes on sporting goods, recreational vehicles and golf course use.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question AND yes votes >= 30% of total ballots cast at the state election (Mass. Const. amend. art. 48) 30% rule: YES must win a majority AND YES votes must equal at least 30% of all ballots cast on Nov 3 (ballots left blank on the question still count in the denominator)

source.criteriaNote: This portfolio has no resolution description. Approval is inferred from the question and answer; cancellation and certification rules are unspecified.

aliases: Initiative Petition for a Law to Protect Water & Nature - Version A
measures.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would create a fund that could be utilized for natural resource conservation that would receive some state taxes collected on the sale and use of sporting goods and recreational vehicles, and the use of golf courses.
measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would not create this natural resource conservation fund or change how sales and use taxes are spent.

measures.title: Single Family Homes
measures.shortSummary: Allows single-family homes on residentially zoned lots of 5,000 square feet or more, subject to reasonable local regulation of certain features, overriding larger local minimum-lot-size rules.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question AND yes votes >= 30% of total ballots cast at the state election (Mass. Const. amend. art. 48) 30% rule: YES must win a majority AND YES votes must equal at least 30% of all ballots cast on Nov 3 (ballots left blank on the question still count in the denominator)

source.criteriaNote: This portfolio has no resolution description. Approval is inferred from the question and answer; cancellation and certification rules are unspecified.

aliases: Initiative Petition for a Law to Allow Single-Family Homes on Small Lots in Areas with Adequate Infrastructure
measures.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would allow single-family homes to be built on lots of 5,000 square feet or more in residential areas, subject to reasonable local regulation of certain aspects of those homes.
measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would make no change to the law relative to building single-family homes.

measures.title: Prohibit Retail Sale of Adult Recreational Use Marijuana
measures.shortSummary: Repeals legalization, regulation and taxation of retail adult-use marijuana sales while keeping medical marijuana and allowing limited personal possession, and changes possession penalties.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question AND yes votes >= 30% of total ballots cast at the state election (Mass. Const. amend. art. 48) 30% rule: YES must win a majority AND YES votes must equal at least 30% of all ballots cast on Nov 3 (ballots left blank on the question still count in the denominator)

source.criteriaNote: This portfolio has no resolution description. Approval is inferred from the question and answer; cancellation and certification rules are unspecified.

aliases: Initiative Petition for a Law Relative to Regulating Marijuana - Version B
measures.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would prohibit the legalization, regulation, and taxation of the retail sale of adult recreational use marijuana, and change the penalties for possession of marijuana.
measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would make no change to the law relative to marijuana.

measures.title: Firearms Regulation
measures.shortSummary: Referendum on keeping the 2024 gun law (Chapter 135 of the Acts of 2024) regulating ghost guns, machine-gun conversion devices and assault-style weapons. YES keeps the law; NO repeals it.
measures.approvalRule: Law stays in effect unless NO wins a majority of votes on the question AND NO votes are >= 30% of total ballots cast (Mass. Const. amend. art. 48, referendum provisions) 30% rule applies to repeal: a NO majority repeals the law only if NO votes equal at least 30% of all ballots cast on Nov 3
aliases: Vote Yes for a Safe Massachusetts
measures.yesMeans: A YES VOTE would keep in place the law, which increases the regulation of firearms, including ghost guns, machine guns, and assault-style weapons.
measures.noMeans: A NO VOTE would repeal this law.
measures.marketNote: The existing market asks whether the gun law is upheld. That can differ from a Yes majority because repeal also needs 30% of all ballots cast. Market criteria need clarification.

measures.title: Arbitration Reform for State Employees Act of 2026
measures.shortSummary: Requires the Governor's budget to fund wages, benefits and other terms in state-employee collective bargaining agreements, whether reached by agreement or ordered by a neutral arbitrator.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Md. Const. art. XIV, sec. 1)
aliases: State Employee Collective Bargaining and Budget Amendment
measures.yesMeans: The Governor must include money in the proposed State budget to pay for agreements with State employees (wages, hours, benefits, other terms), whether negotiated or decided by a neutral decision-maker.
measures.noMeans: The law about funding agreements between the State and State employees stays the same.

measures.title: Temporary Appointments on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities
measures.shortSummary: Allows temporary substitute members on the Commission on Judicial Disabilities when a member is recused, disqualified, or their term expires without a replacement.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Md. Const. art. XIV, sec. 1)
aliases: Commission on Judicial Disabilities Vacancies Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Temporary appointments allowed: the Commission Chair may recall a former member, or the Governor (at the Chair's request) may appoint a substitute or extend a member's term until a replacement is appointed.
measures.noMeans: Current membership rules stay the same; no temporary appointments when a member is recused, disqualified, or a term ends.

measures.title: Electoral Districts - General Assembly and Congressional Representatives
measures.shortSummary: Limits certain state-constitution districting rules to state legislative districts, lets the legislature give the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction over congressional maps, and says the constitution sets no congressional boundary criteria.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Md. Const. art. XIV, sec. 1)
measures.yesMeans: Amends Art. III so the listed districting requirements apply only to Senate/House of Delegates districts, authorizes original Supreme Court jurisdiction over the congressional plan, and provides no state-constitutional criteria for congressional boundaries.
measures.noMeans: Maryland Constitution's districting provisions stay as they are.

measures.title: A proposal to convene a constitutional convention for the purpose of drafting a general revision of the state constitution
measures.shortSummary: Constitutionally required every-16-years question: should elected delegates convene in 2027 to draft a general revision of Michigan's constitution, to be submitted to voters later?
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Mich. Const. art. XII, sec. 3)
measures.yesMeans: Delegates would be elected and a convention convened (2027) to draft a revised constitution, which would then go to voters for approval or rejection.
measures.noMeans: No constitutional convention is called.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: A proposed initiated law to prohibit campaign contributions from certain regulated utilities and government contractors and apply campaign finance laws and regulations to additional types of political communications
measures.shortSummary: Bans campaign contributions from regulated electric and gas utilities, contractors with over $250,000 a year in government contracts, and closely connected people or groups; extends disclosure rules to ads naming candidates or ballot questions.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Mich. Const. art. II, sec. 9); once adopted, the Legislature can amend it only by a 3/4 vote of each house
aliases: Michiganders for Money Out of Politics
DTE and Consumers Energy donations ban
measures.yesMeans: Adopts the initiated law: contribution ban for covered utilities, contractors and connected persons; broader disclosure for political communications, including internet communications.
measures.noMeans: Current campaign finance law stays the same.

measures.title: Increasing funding to school districts. Shall the Minnesota Constitution be amended to increase the funding going to all school districts from the permanent school fund, which is a fund that supports school districts without raising individual income or property taxes, effective July 1, 2027?
measures.shortSummary: Changes how the Permanent School Fund is managed and paid out: preserve purchasing power and set distributions by law; companion statute sets an annual distribution of 4.5% of the 3-year average net asset value.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of ALL voters who cast a ballot in the election, not just those voting on the question (Minn. Const. art. IX, sec. 1) YES votes must exceed 50% of total ballots cast in the Nov 3 election; a blank or skipped answer has the same effect as NO (SOS: 'Failure to vote on a constitutional amendment will have the same effect as voting no on the amendment').
aliases: Alter Investment and Distribution Policies for Permanent School Fund Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Amends Art. XI sec. 8 so the fund is managed as a perpetual resource preserving purchasing power, with distributions set by law; linked statutes take effect July 1, 2027 (4.5% annual distributable amount).
measures.noMeans: Art. XI sec. 8 unchanged; the fund keeps being invested for maximum return consistent with perpetuity, with income-based distributions.

measures.title: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: Repeal the 2024 voter-approved Amendment providing reproductive healthcare rights, including abortion through fetal viability; Allow abortions for rape and incest (under twelve-weeks' gestation), emergencies, and fetal anomalies; Allow legislation regulating abortion; Ensure parental consent for minors' abortions; Prohibit gender transition procedures for minors?
measures.shortSummary: Legislative amendment repealing the 2024 abortion-rights provision (Art. I, Sec. 36); allows abortion only for emergencies, fetal anomalies, and rape/incest under 12 weeks; permits abortion regulation and parental consent; bans gender-transition procedures for minors.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Mo. Const. art. XII, sec. 2(b)); takes effect 30 days after the election.
aliases: Prohibit Abortion and Gender Transition Procedures for Minors Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Fair ballot language: repeals Art. I Sec. 36 (2024); allows restricting abortion to medical emergency, rape/incest under 12 weeks, and fetal anomalies; allows regulation of providers; requires informed consent incl. parental/judicial consent for minors; bars public funding (limited exceptions); prohibits gender transition procedures for minors.
measures.noMeans: Fair ballot language: leaves Art. I Sec. 36 (2024) in place; abortion stays available through fetal viability; no ban on gender transition procedures for minors.

measures.title: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to: expand the initiative and referendum petition process by making it a fundamental right; allow courts to revise ballot summaries through lawsuits; prohibit the legislature from weakening initiative or referendum powers; prohibit the legislature from changing or repealing laws enacted through the initiative process, or passing laws similar to those rejected by referendum, without approval from at least 80% of both chambers; and preserve existing majority vote and signature requirements for initiative and referendum petitions?
measures.shortSummary: Citizen initiative making initiative/referendum a fundamental right; bars weakening those powers; changes to initiative-enacted laws, or re-passing referendum-rejected laws, need 80% of both chambers and referral to voters; keeps current signature and majority rules.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Mo. Const. art. XII, sec. 2(b)); effective 30 days after election. No district-majority rule (Aug 4, 2026 Amendment 4 proposing one was rejected).
aliases: Initiative and Referendum Powers and Legislative Change Requirements Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Fair ballot language: legislature cannot directly amend initiative-enacted laws; changes must be referred to voters by at least 80% of each chamber; legislature restricted from limiting initiatives/referenda; keeps 5%/8% signature rules and simple statewide majority.
measures.noMeans: Fair ballot language: no change to current constitutional provisions, which already give citizens the right to propose initiatives and referenda.

measures.title: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to establish a permanent public endowment fund to support state government instead of taxing Missouri residents, prohibit the General Assembly from appropriating or diverting the fund, and eliminate state-imposed taxes once the fund generates sufficient revenue to replace them?
measures.shortSummary: Creates the 'Show-Me Prosperity Fund,' a permanent endowment; no appropriations until earnings can replace state taxes, then capped at 3% of 5-year average value; eliminated state taxes can't be reimposed unless the fund fails.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Mo. Const. art. XII, sec. 2(b)); effective 30 days after election.
aliases: Creation of Show-Me Prosperity Investment Fund for State Tax Reduction and Elimination Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Fair ballot language: establishes the Show-Me Prosperity Fund to eliminate state-imposed taxes; no appropriation until Treasurer certifies earnings suffice; 3% annual draw cap; bars re-enacting eliminated taxes, except legislature may tax/appropriate if fund becomes insolvent or fails.
measures.noMeans: Fair ballot language: no permanent public endowment fund is established.

measures.title: Shall the Missouri Constitution be amended to support law enforcement by preserving the right of citizens to elect a county sheriff, prohibiting the removal of a county sheriff except by a writ of quo warranto, and recognizing the office of sheriff as part of the administration of justice?
measures.shortSummary: Puts county sheriffs in the Constitution: counties must elect a sheriff every four years, sheriff duties now in statute are constitutionalized, and an elected sheriff can be removed only by quo warranto brought by the Attorney General.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Mo. Const. art. XII, sec. 2(b)); effective 30 days after election.
aliases: Require Election of County Sheriffs Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Fair ballot language: requires counties to elect a sheriff every four years (now statutory); places sheriff duties in the Constitution; elected sheriff removable only by writ of quo warranto initiated by the Attorney General.
measures.noMeans: Fair ballot language: no constitutional change; statutes on sheriff elections (4-year terms), duties and removal stay in effect unless changed by law.

measures.title: Do the people of the state of Missouri approve the act of the General Assembly entitled 'House Bill No. 1 (2025 Second Extraordinary Session),' which repeals Missouri's existing congressional plan, and replaces it with new congressional boundaries that keep more counties intact?
measures.shortSummary: Referendum on HB 1 (2025 Second Extraordinary Session), the mid-decade congressional map replacing the 2022 districts. YES approves the 2025 map for future elections; NO rejects it, keeping the 2022 map. Nov 2026 House races use the 2022 map regardless.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (Mo. Const. art. III, sec. 52(b): 'shall take effect when approved by a majority of the votes cast thereon, and not otherwise').

source.criteriaNote: Pass means voters approve the 2025 congressional map. Fail means they reject it.

measures.yesMeans: Official: "A 'yes' vote will approve the act of the General Assembly entitled 'House Bill No. 1 (2025 Extraordinary Session),' which redraws the congressional district boundaries." Per Mo. Sup. Ct. (SC101805), HB 1 then takes effect 30 days after the election (future elections, not 2026).
measures.noMeans: Official: "A 'no' vote will leave in place the congressional district boundaries enacted in 2022." HB 1 never takes effect (art. III sec. 52(b): referred measure takes effect only if approved).

measures.title: CI-132 amends the Montana Constitution to require that judicial elections remain nonpartisan.
measures.shortSummary: Adds Article VII, Section 12 to the Montana Constitution: 'Judicial elections shall remain nonpartisan.'
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (Mont. Const. art. XIV §9)
measures.yesMeans: Judicial elections must stay nonpartisan under the constitution.
measures.noMeans: Nonpartisan judicial elections remain a matter of statute that the Legislature could change.

measures.title: CI-133 amends the constitution to secure the fundamental right of initiative and referendum from interference by the government.
measures.shortSummary: Adds the initiative and referendum powers to Montana's Declaration of Rights, requiring timely, impartial ballot-issue processes, limits on technical petition rejections, signature withdrawal, and no government resources for or against measures.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (Mont. Const. art. XIV §9)
measures.yesMeans: Initiative/referendum becomes a fundamental right (Art. II §37) subject to strict scrutiny, with process guarantees.
measures.noMeans: Initiative and referendum process continues under current constitution and statutes.

measures.title: Initiative No. 194 - The Montana Plan Act
measures.shortSummary: Redefines powers of corporations, nonprofits and other 'artificial persons' to exclude contributing to candidate elections, parties or ballot issues; violators forfeit privileges to do business in Montana.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure
measures.yesMeans: Artificial persons lose the legal power to spend on candidates, parties or ballot issues in Montana.
measures.noMeans: Current law on entity political spending stays in place.

measures.designation: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT - MAXIMUM INCOME TAX RATE OF 3.5% (unnumbered; ballot header 'Constitutional Amendment')
measures.title: Lower Taxes for All NC
measures.shortSummary: Lowers the constitutional ceiling on North Carolina's income tax rate from 7% to 3.5%, for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (N.C. Const. art. XIII §4)
aliases: Reduce Income Tax Rate Cap from 7% to 3.5% Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Maximum allowable State income tax rate drops from 7% to 3.5% beginning Jan 1, 2027 (official LSO summary).
measures.noMeans: 7% constitutional cap remains.

measures.designation: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT - PROPERTY TAX LEVY LIMIT (unnumbered; ballot header 'Constitutional Amendment')
measures.title: Property Tax Levy Limit
measures.shortSummary: Requires the General Assembly to enact general laws limiting how much local governments' property tax levies may increase; the specific limit and any exceptions would be set by statute.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (N.C. Const. art. XIII §4)
measures.yesMeans: General Assembly must set limits on property tax increases by local governments (official LSO summary).
measures.noMeans: No constitutional requirement for property tax levy limits.

measures.designation: CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT - REQUIRE PHOTO ID FOR VOTING (unnumbered; ballot header 'Constitutional Amendment')
measures.title: Require Photo ID for All Voters
measures.shortSummary: Extends the constitution's photo-ID requirement, adopted in 2018 for in-person voters only, to all voters regardless of voting method, including absentee/mail voters.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (N.C. Const. art. XIII §4)
aliases: Require Photo ID for All Voters Constitutional Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Constitution would require photo identification from all voters before voting, not just in-person voters (official LSO summary).
measures.noMeans: Constitutional photo-ID mandate stays limited to in-person voting; existing statutes unchanged.

measures.title: Constitutional Measure No. 1 (House Concurrent Resolution No. 3003, 2025 Session Laws, Ch. 614)
measures.shortSummary: Requires future constitutional amendments, whether referred by the Legislature or initiated by petition, to receive at least 60% of votes cast on the question.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (SOS guide: 'a majority vote would result in passage')
measures.yesMeans: Future constitutional amendments would need at least 60% approval (SOS guide).
measures.noMeans: Constitutional amendments continue to need more than 50% (SOS guide).

measures.title: Initiated Constitutional Measure No. 2 (funding of school lunches; new section to Article VIII)
measures.shortSummary: Requires public schools to provide one free breakfast and lunch each school day to all students, with the state reimbursing costs, adjusted for inflation, from legacy fund earnings if no other source is identified.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure (SOS guide: 'a majority vote would result in passage')
measures.yesMeans: State funds one free breakfast and lunch daily for students at participating schools (SOS guide).
measures.noMeans: No state funding beyond current free and reduced-price meal eligibility (SOS guide).

measures.title: Fairness for Girls: Shall the Nebraska Constitution be amended to provide: (1) Schools must expressly designate each athletic team or sport as one of the following based on biological sex: (a) Males, men, or boys; (b) females, women, or girls; or (c) coed or mixed; and (2) Athletic teams or sports designated for females, women, or girls shall not be open to students of the male sex?
measures.shortSummary: Adds Art. VII sec. 16 requiring schools and colleges to designate teams as male, female or coed by biological sex and barring male students from female teams; covers public schools and private schools competing against them.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the measure AND 'For' votes >= 35% of total votes cast at the election (Neb. Const. art. III, sec. 4) 35% rule: even with a majority, 'For' votes must equal at least 35% of all voters casting ballots in the Nov 3 election (e.g., 100 voters -> at least 35 'For')
measures.yesMeans: A vote 'FOR' will amend the Nebraska Constitution to require sex-based team designations and close female teams to students of the male sex, at public schools/colleges and private schools that compete against them.
measures.noMeans: A vote 'AGAINST' means the Nebraska Constitution will not be amended in this manner.

measures.title: Online Sports Wagering Authorization: Shall the Nebraska Constitution be amended to authorize the enactment of laws allowing persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform when offered by an authorized gaming operator conducting games of chance within a licensed racetrack enclosure in Nebraska?
measures.shortSummary: Amends Art. III sec. 24 so laws may allow people located in Nebraska to bet on sports online through platforms offered by licensed racetrack-casino gaming operators.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the measure AND 'For' votes >= 35% of total votes cast at the election (Neb. Const. art. III, sec. 4) 35% rule: even with a majority, 'For' votes must equal at least 35% of all voters casting ballots in the Nov 3 election (e.g., 100 voters -> at least 35 'For')
measures.yesMeans: A vote 'FOR' will amend the Nebraska Constitution to authorize laws allowing persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform offered by an authorized racetrack gaming operator.
measures.noMeans: A vote 'AGAINST' means the Nebraska Constitution will not be amended in this manner.

measures.title: Online Sports Wagering Regulation: Shall statutes be enacted that: (1) Allow persons located within Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform when offered by an authorized gaming operator conducting games of chance within a licensed racetrack enclosure in Nebraska or the operator's platform provider; and (2) Regulate such sports wagers?
measures.shortSummary: Enacts statutes under the Racetrack Gaming Act letting licensed racetrack gaming operators or their platform providers offer online sports wagering to people in Nebraska, and regulating it; operative Jan 1, 2027.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the measure AND 'For' votes >= 35% of total votes cast at the election (Neb. Const. art. III, sec. 4) 35% rule: even with a majority, 'For' votes must equal at least 35% of all voters casting ballots in the Nov 3 election (e.g., 100 voters -> at least 35 'For')
measures.yesMeans: A vote 'FOR' will enact statutes allowing persons in Nebraska to place sports wagers through an Internet-based platform offered by an authorized racetrack gaming operator or its platform provider, and regulating such wagers.
measures.noMeans: A vote 'AGAINST' means no such statutes will be enacted.

measures.title: A constitutional amendment to change the limit on legislative terms from two consecutive terms to three consecutive terms.
measures.shortSummary: Amends Art. III sec. 12 to let state senators serve three consecutive four-year terms (12 years) instead of two before a four-year break.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the amendment AND 'For' votes >= 35% of total votes cast at the election (Neb. Const. art. XVI, sec. 1) 35% rule: even with a majority, 'For' votes must equal at least 35% of all voters casting ballots in the Nov 3 election (e.g., 100 voters -> at least 35 'For')
measures.yesMeans: A vote FOR will amend the state constitution to increase the term limit for state legislators from two consecutive four-year terms (eight years) to three consecutive four-year terms (12 years).
measures.noMeans: A vote AGAINST will not amend the Nebraska Constitution, so the current limit of two consecutive four-year terms will remain in effect.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: Are you in favor of eliminating the office of register of probate by amending articles 71 and 81 of the second part of the constitution...?
measures.shortSummary: Deletes the elected county office of register of probate and all references to it from Part 2, Articles 71 and 81 of the New Hampshire Constitution.
measures.approvalRule: Two-thirds (66.67%) of votes cast on the question (N.H. Const. pt. 2, art. 100); ballots with no oval marked are not counted on the question
aliases: Eliminate Office of Register of Probate Amendment
measures.yesMeans: If the amendment is adopted, the constitution will eliminate the position of register of probate.
measures.noMeans: Registers of probate remain constitutional county offices.
measures.marketNote: No linked market yet · ballot details or market criteria under review.

measures.title: The 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act authorizes the issuance and sale of higher education, special schools and tribal schools capital improvement and acquisition bonds.
measures.shortSummary: Authorizes up to $352,225,379 in general obligation bonds for higher education, special schools and tribal schools capital improvements and acquisitions, repaid by a statewide property tax levy.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. IX §8)
measures.yesMeans: 'For' authorizes the $352.2M higher education bonds.
measures.noMeans: 'Against' denies authority to issue these bonds.

measures.title: Proposing to amend Article 4, Section 10 of the Constitution of New Mexico to allow legislative compensation that is limited to the median household income for New Mexico, to require legislative compensation to be reduced if the median household income for New Mexico falls, to allow legislative compensation to be increased only if the median household income for New Mexico rises and to provide for delayed implementation.
measures.shortSummary: Allows the Legislature to pay legislators a salary capped at New Mexico's median household income (about $68,000 in 2026), adjusting with that median, starting with the legislature seated in 2029.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. XIX §1); SOS guide: none of the 2026 amendments needs the three-fourths supermajority
measures.yesMeans: Legislators may receive a salary up to the state median household income, from 2029.
measures.noMeans: Legislators continue to receive only per diem and mileage.

measures.title: The 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act authorizes the issuance and sale of library acquisition bonds.
measures.shortSummary: Authorizes up to $19,324,188 in general obligation bonds for academic, public school, public and tribal library resource acquisitions, repaid by a statewide property tax levy.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. IX §8)
measures.yesMeans: 'For' authorizes the $19.32M library bonds.
measures.noMeans: 'Against' denies authority to issue these bonds.

measures.title: Proposing an amendment to Article 4, Section 22 of the Constitution of New Mexico to require the governor to provide veto messages on all bills vetoed in whole or in part and to provide that all bills passed by the legislature and not acted on by the governor will become law.
measures.shortSummary: Ends the governor's pocket veto so bills not acted on become law, and requires veto messages for all bills vetoed in whole or in part.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. XIX §1); SOS guide: none of the 2026 amendments needs the three-fourths supermajority
measures.yesMeans: Bills the governor does not act on become law; veto explanations required.
measures.noMeans: Governor keeps the pocket veto for bills presented in the session's last three days.

measures.title: Proposing an amendment to Article 12, Section 13 of the Constitution of New Mexico to establish nominating committees to provide lists of nominees to the governor for appointment of nonstudent members to the boards of regents of state educational institutions; student members from a list by an elected student governing body; party-registration-change restriction.
measures.shortSummary: Creates nominating committees that give the governor candidate lists for nonstudent university regents, has student regents chosen from student-government lists, and bars recent party-registration changes by nonstudent regents.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. XIX §1); SOS guide: none of the 2026 amendments needs the three-fourths supermajority
measures.yesMeans: Governor must appoint nonstudent regents from nominating-committee lists.
measures.noMeans: Governor keeps current regent appointment discretion with Senate confirmation.

measures.title: Proposing to amend Article 7, Section 1 of the Constitution of New Mexico to remove the requirement that school elections be separate from partisan elections.
measures.shortSummary: Removes the constitutional rule that school elections be held at different times from partisan elections, allowing school bond and levy questions on general-election ballots.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. XIX §1); SOS guide: none of the 2026 amendments needs the three-fourths supermajority (despite amending art. VII §1, a section listed in art. XIX §1's 3/4 rule)
measures.yesMeans: School elections/questions may be held with partisan elections.
measures.noMeans: School elections must remain separate from partisan elections.

measures.title: The 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act authorizes the issuance and sale of senior citizen facility improvement, construction and equipment acquisition bonds.
measures.shortSummary: Authorizes up to $21,582,213 in general obligation bonds for senior citizen facility improvement, construction and equipment, repaid by a statewide property tax levy.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (N.M. Const. art. IX §8)
aliases: 2026 Capital Projects General Obligation Bond Act
measures.yesMeans: 'For' authorizes the $21.58M senior facility bonds.
measures.noMeans: 'Against' denies authority to issue these bonds.

measures.title: Should the Nevada Constitution be amended to create an individual's fundamental right to an abortion, without interference by state or local governments, whenever the abortion is performed by a qualified healthcare professional until fetal viability or when necessary to protect the health or life of the pregnant individual at any point during the pregnancy?
measures.shortSummary: Adds a state constitutional right to abortion until fetal viability, or later when needed to protect the patient's life or health; second required vote after 2024 approval.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question at each of two consecutive general elections (Nev. Const. art. 19 §2(4)). Initiated constitutional amendments must pass at two consecutive general elections; 2026 is the second and final vote (first approved 2024-11-05 as Question 6, ~64.4% yes).
measures.yesMeans: Adds Art. 1 §25 creating a fundamental right to abortion until fetal viability or when needed to protect the patient's life or health.
measures.noMeans: The amendment fails and is not added to the constitution despite its 2024 approval.

measures.title: Should the Nevada Constitution be amended to require voters to either present photo identification to verify their identity when voting in-person or to provide certain personal information to verify their identity when voting by mail ballot?
measures.shortSummary: Constitutional amendment requiring photo ID for in-person voting and the last four digits of a driver's license or Social Security number for mail ballots; second required vote after 2024.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question at each of two consecutive general elections (Nev. Const. art. 19 §2(4)). Initiated constitutional amendments must pass at two consecutive general elections; 2026 is the second and final vote (first approved 2024-11-05 as Question 7, ~73.2% yes).
measures.yesMeans: Adds Art. 2 §§1B–1C requiring photo ID to vote in person and ID-number verification for mail ballots.
measures.noMeans: The amendment fails and is not added to the constitution despite its 2024 approval.

measures.title: Voters to present photo identification in order to vote (Proposed by Joint Resolution of the General Assembly; to enact Section 5 of Article V of the Ohio Constitution)
measures.shortSummary: Adds Ohio's photo-ID voting requirement to the state constitution: in-person voters must show listed government-issued photo ID, with a religious-objection alternative; absentee voters must provide ID or other identifiers allowed by law.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the issue (ballot: 'A majority yes vote is required for the adoption of Section 5'; Ohio Const. art. XVI, sec. 1)
measures.yesMeans: Constitution would require approved government-issued photo ID to vote (unexpired Ohio license/state ID, US passport/card, military/National Guard/VA ID), with a law-defined alternative for sincere religious objectors.
measures.noMeans: No constitutional change; Ohio's existing statutory photo-ID requirement (since 2023) remains in law.

measures.title: SQ 845, LR 379 Final Ballot Title (Judicial Nominating Commission), as rewritten by the Attorney General
measures.shortSummary: Restructures the 15-member Judicial Nominating Commission: governor and Oklahoma Bar each appoint six (one per current congressional district), three at-large; allows attorney members, removes most party limits, changes terms.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (Okla. Const. art. XXIV §1)
measures.yesMeans: Amends art. 7-B §3 to restructure JNC appointments, terms and party/attorney rules.
measures.noMeans: JNC keeps its current structure based on 1967 congressional districts.

measures.title: SQ 847, LR 381 Final Ballot Title (Real property valuation), as rewritten by the Attorney General
measures.shortSummary: Lowers caps on annual growth in taxable fair cash value from 2027 to 4% (most property) and 1.75% (homesteads, farmland), and replaces the senior freeze income cap with income-tiered limits.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the question (Okla. Const. art. XXIV §1)
measures.yesMeans: Amends art. 10 §§8B-8C: 4%/1.75% caps; seniors at or below area median income get no increase; tiered caps above.
measures.noMeans: Keeps 5%/3% caps and the current income-capped senior valuation freeze.

measures.title: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution that Repeals Expanded Medicaid Coverage if Federal Funding for the Program Drops below 90%.
measures.shortSummary: Ends South Dakota's voter-approved Medicaid expansion (2022 Amendment D) if the federal share of expansion costs falls below 90%.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (S.D. Const. art. XXIII)
measures.yesMeans: Adopts the amendment (AG pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: Leaves the Constitution as it is (AG pamphlet).

measures.title: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution Clarifying that an Individual Must Be a Citizen of the United States to be Eligible to Vote.
measures.shortSummary: Adds non-U.S. citizens to the list of people disqualified from voting in the state constitution, clarifying the existing citizenship requirement.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (S.D. Const. art. XXIII)
measures.yesMeans: Adopts the amendment (AG pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: Leaves the Constitution as it is (AG pamphlet).

measures.title: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution Establishing the Trust for Unclaimed Property Fund.
measures.shortSummary: Creates a constitutional trust fund for abandoned unclaimed property, with portions of interest and income distributed to the general fund as the Legislature sets.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (S.D. Const. art. XXIII)
measures.yesMeans: Adopts the amendment (AG pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: Leaves the Constitution as it is (AG pamphlet).

measures.title: An Amendment to the South Dakota Constitution Requiring that a Proposed Constitutional Amendment or Revision Receive an Affirmative Vote of Sixty Percent of the Votes Cast.
measures.shortSummary: Requires future constitutional amendments or revisions to receive 60% of the votes cast to take effect, instead of a simple majority.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (S.D. Const. art. XXIII); L itself needs only a simple majority
measures.yesMeans: Adopts the amendment; future amendments need 60% (AG pamphlet).
measures.noMeans: Leaves the Constitution as it is; majority approval continues (AG pamphlet).

measures.title: Proposed amendment to Article I, Section 15 (bail)
measures.shortSummary: Allows courts to deny pretrial bail, when proof is evident or presumption great, for capital offenses, terrorism, second-degree murder, aggravated rape (incl. of a child), grave torture, and 85%-sentence offenses; judges must state reasons on the record.
measures.approvalRule: Two prongs (Tenn. Const. art. XI §3: 'by a majority of all the citizens of the State voting for Governor, voting in their favor'): (1) more YES than NO votes; (2) YES votes > half of all votes cast for governor (50% + 1). YES must exceed 50% of total gubernatorial votes (sum of all governor candidates / 2); undervotes on the amendment effectively count against it. Method upheld in George v. Hargett, 879 F.3d 711 (6th Cir. 2018).
aliases: Remove Right to Bail for Certain Criminal Offenses Measure
measures.yesMeans: Bail may be denied for the listed offenses; courts must record reasons for granting or denying bail in those cases.
measures.noMeans: Art. I §15 unchanged: bail denial limited to capital offenses.

measures.title: Proposed amendment to Article II, Section 28 (prohibit state property tax)
measures.shortSummary: Adds language to Article II, Section 28 prohibiting the Legislature from levying, authorizing or otherwise permitting any state tax on real, personal or mixed property.
measures.approvalRule: Two prongs (Tenn. Const. art. XI §3): (1) more YES than NO; (2) YES votes > half of all votes cast for governor. YES must exceed 50% of total gubernatorial votes; upheld in George v. Hargett (6th Cir. 2018).
measures.yesMeans: Constitution bars any state-level property tax.
measures.noMeans: Art. II §28 unchanged; no constitutional ban on a state property tax.

measures.title: Proposed amendment to Article I, Section 35 (rights of crime victims)
measures.shortSummary: Replaces Article I, Section 35 with an expanded list of crime victims' rights (Marsy's Law), including fair treatment, parole participation, protection from harassment, notice of release dates and safety consideration before release.
measures.approvalRule: Two prongs (Tenn. Const. art. XI §3): (1) more YES than NO; (2) YES votes > half of all votes cast for governor. YES must exceed 50% of total gubernatorial votes; upheld in George v. Hargett (6th Cir. 2018).
aliases: Marsy's Law Crime Victims' Rights Measure
measures.yesMeans: Victims' rights section rewritten with 13 enumerated rights; no new damages claim against the state; prosecutor/court powers not restricted.
measures.noMeans: Current Art. I §35 victims' rights remain.

measures.title: Shall the Utah Constitution be amended to require that citizen-proposed laws that increase taxes compared to existing law be approved by at least 60% of voters, instead of a simple majority?
measures.shortSummary: Requires statewide citizen initiatives that create, expand or raise a tax (or shrink a property-tax rate decrease) to win at least 60% voter approval, for initiatives voted on after Nov 1, 2026.
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Utah Const. art. XXIII §1: 'a majority of the electors voting thereon')
aliases: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Statewide Initiatives
measures.yesMeans: Tax-increasing statewide initiatives would need at least 60% approval.
measures.noMeans: Tax-related initiatives continue to need a simple majority.

measures.title: Shall the Utah Constitution be amended to change how proposed constitutional amendments are published, requiring publication for 60 days immediately before the general election in a manner established by state law instead of in newspapers?
measures.shortSummary: Replaces the requirement to publish proposed constitutional amendments in newspapers in every county with 60-day publication before the election in a manner set by law (online via H.B. 481).
measures.approvalRule: Simple majority of votes cast on the amendment (Utah Const. art. XXIII §1: 'a majority of the electors voting thereon')
aliases: Proposal to Amend Utah Constitution - Publication Amendments
measures.yesMeans: Lt. Governor publishes amendments and legislative ballot questions online (Utah Public Notice Website and LG site) for 60 days; H.B. 481 takes effect.
measures.noMeans: Newspaper publication in each county for two months before the election continues.

measures.title: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) protect the freedom to make personal decisions about prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, birth control, abortion, miscarriage management, and fertility care; (ii) protect doctors, nurses, and patients from being punished for these decisions; and (iii) allow for restrictions on access to abortion during the third trimester of pregnancy except when the patient's health is at risk or the pregnancy cannot survive?
measures.shortSummary: Adds a fundamental right to reproductive freedom (Art. I, Sec. 11-A) covering prenatal care, contraception, abortion, miscarriage and fertility care; state may regulate third-trimester abortion but must allow it for patient life/health or nonviable fetus.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of those voting on the amendment (Va. Const. art. XII, sec. 1); takes effect on the date the General Assembly prescribed when submitting it.
measures.yesMeans: Adds Art. I Sec. 11-A: right to make and carry out own reproductive-care decisions, burdened only by a narrowly defined compelling health interest; third-trimester abortion may be regulated but not banned when medically indicated or fetus nonviable; no penalties for patients/helpers (official explanation).
measures.noMeans: Constitution stays silent on reproductive freedom; abortion remains governed by statute (official 'Present Law').

measures.title: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) remove the ban on same-sex marriage; (ii) affirm that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race; and (iii) require all legally valid marriages to be treated equally under the law?
measures.shortSummary: Replaces the 2006 constitutional ban on same-sex marriage (Art. I, Sec. 15-A) with a right to marry: the state must license, recognize and treat equally lawful marriages of two adults regardless of sex, gender or race.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of those voting on the amendment (Va. Const. art. XII, sec. 1).
aliases: Remove Constitutional Same-Sex Marriage Ban Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Removes the one-man-one-woman marriage ban from Art. I Sec. 15-A; adds that marriage is a vital personal right; state may not deny a license to two adults based on sex, gender or race and must recognize such marriages equally (official explanation).
measures.noMeans: Ban stays in the Constitution; unenforceable under Obergefell v. Hodges (2015) but would become enforceable again if that decision were overturned (official 'Present Law').

measures.title: Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended (i) to provide for the fundamental right to vote in the Commonwealth, (ii) to revise the qualifications of voters so that a person convicted of a felony is not entitled to vote during his period of incarceration but is automatically invested with the right to vote upon release from incarceration, and (iii) to update the existing prohibition on voting by persons found to be mentally incompetent to instead apply to persons who have been found to lack the capacity to understand the act of voting?
measures.shortSummary: Makes voting a fundamental right; people convicted of felonies lose the vote only while incarcerated and regain it automatically on release (no Governor restoration); disqualification for incapacity requires a court finding of inability to understand voting.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of those voting on the amendment (Va. Const. art. XII, sec. 1).
aliases: Voting Rights Restoration for Felons Upon Release Amendment
measures.yesMeans: Amends Art. II Sec. 1: fundamental right to vote; felony disqualification only during incarceration, rights (vote, jury, office, notary) restored automatically on release; incapacity bar limited to court finding person cannot understand act of voting (official explanation).
measures.noMeans: Felony conviction keeps a lifetime voting ban unless the Governor individually restores rights; broad 'mentally incompetent' disqualification remains (official 'Present Law').

measures.title: Proposal 3: Article 23 of Chapter I [Right to collectively bargain]
measures.shortSummary: Adds a constitutional right for employees to organize or join a union and bargain collectively through an exclusive representative; bars laws that interfere with that right or prohibit union-security (membership-required) agreements.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the proposal (Vt. Const. ch. II, sec. 72)
measures.yesMeans: Adds Ch. I Art. 23 guaranteeing the right to collectively bargain over wages, hours and working conditions; no law may diminish it or bar membership-required union agreements.
measures.noMeans: Vermont Constitution unchanged.

measures.title: Proposal 4: Article 23 of Chapter I [Equality of rights]
measures.shortSummary: Guarantees equal protection under the law and bars the state from denying equal treatment based on race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or national origin.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the proposal (Vt. Const. ch. II, sec. 72)
measures.yesMeans: Adds Ch. I Art. 23 guaranteeing equal protection; allows measures meant to provide equality for historically disadvantaged groups.
measures.noMeans: Vermont Constitution unchanged.

measures.title: Initiative Measure No. IL26-001 concerns parental rights relating to their children in public school.
measures.shortSummary: Repeals 2025 amendments to the public-school parents' rights statute (RCW 28A.605.005) and re-enacts it as originally passed via Initiative 2081 in 2024.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the measure, provided votes on it equal ≥1/3 of all votes cast at the election (Wash. Const. art. II §1(d)); effective 30th day after election (2026-12-03). Votes cast on the measure must equal at least one-third of total votes cast at the election (Wash. Const. art. II §1(d)).
measures.yesMeans: Repeals the 2025 amendments and restores RCW 28A.605.005 (parent/guardian rights list) as enacted by Initiative 2081 in 2024.
measures.noMeans: The parents' rights statute stays as amended by the 2025 Legislature.

measures.title: Initiative Measure No. IL26-638 concerns participation in athletics at K-12 schools.
measures.shortSummary: Bars students defined as 'biologically male' from girls' school sports and requires a health-care-provider form verifying biological sex to play on female teams.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the measure, provided votes on it equal ≥1/3 of all votes cast at the election (Wash. Const. art. II §1(d)); effective 30th day after election (2026-12-03). Votes cast on the measure must equal at least one-third of total votes cast at the election (Wash. Const. art. II §1(d)).
measures.yesMeans: Prohibits 'biologically male' students from female-only school athletics and requires provider-signed sex verification for female teams.
measures.noMeans: Current sex/gender-identity non-discrimination rules for school sports stay.

measures.title: Initiative Measure No. IP26-645 concerns state and local taxes.
measures.shortSummary: Repeals the 2026 9.9% tax on individual income over $1 million, bars state and local taxes on or measured by individual income, and defines 'income'.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the measure, provided votes on it equal ≥1/3 of all votes cast at the election (Wash. Const. art. II §1(d)); effective 30th day after election (2026-12-03). Votes cast on the measure must equal at least one-third of total votes cast at the election (Wash. Const. art. II §1(d)).
aliases: An Initiative Prohibiting Individual Income Taxes
measures.yesMeans: Repeals the 9.9% tax on income over $1,000,000 and prohibits state and local individual income taxes; related tax breaks in the 2026 law remain.
measures.noMeans: The 9.9% tax on annual individual income over $1 million (ESSB 6346, from 2028) stays in law.

measures.title: Partial veto. Shall section 10 (1) (c) of article V of the constitution be amended to prohibit the governor, in exercising his or her partial veto authority, from creating or increasing or authorizing the creation or increase of any tax or fee?
measures.shortSummary: Bars the governor from using the partial veto on appropriation bills to create or increase any tax or fee, or to authorize such an increase (including by local governments).
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Wis. Const. art. XII, sec. 1)
measures.yesMeans: Amends art. V sec. 10(1)(c) so a partial veto may not create, increase, or authorize creating or increasing any tax or fee.
measures.noMeans: Art. V sec. 10(1)(c) unchanged.

measures.title: Freedom to gather in places of worship during an emergency. Shall section 18 of article I of the constitution, which deals with religious liberty, be amended to prohibit the state or a political subdivision of the state from ordering the closure of, or forbidding gatherings in, places of worship in response to a state of emergency, including a public health emergency?
measures.shortSummary: Bars the state and local governments from closing places of worship or forbidding gatherings in them in response to any declared emergency, including a public health emergency.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Wis. Const. art. XII, sec. 1)
measures.yesMeans: Amends art. I sec. 18 to prohibit state/local orders closing or forbidding gatherings in places of worship during a state of emergency.
measures.noMeans: Art. I sec. 18 unchanged.

measures.title: Governmental entity discrimination prohibited. Shall section 27 of article I of the constitution be created to prohibit governmental entities in the state from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any individual or group on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, public education, public contracting, or public administration?
measures.shortSummary: Creates art. I sec. 27 barring state and local governments, schools and universities from discriminating against or granting preferential treatment based on race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin in employment, education, contracting or administration.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (Wis. Const. art. XII, sec. 1)
measures.yesMeans: Creates art. I sec. 27 prohibiting governmental discrimination or preferential treatment on those bases, with exceptions for federal-funding eligibility, federal law, and bona fide sex-based qualifications.
measures.noMeans: No new constitutional provision is added.

measures.title: Citizenship Requirement to Vote in West Virginia Elections Amendment
measures.shortSummary: Amends W. Va. Const. art. IV §1 to provide that only citizens of the United States who are citizens of West Virginia are entitled to vote in all elections held in the state.
measures.approvalRule: Majority of votes cast on the question (W. Va. Const. art. XIV §2; W. Va. Code §3-11-6)
aliases: Citizenship Requirement to Vote in West Virginia Elections Amendment
measures.yesMeans: For Ratification: 'This amendment provides that in all elections held in West Virginia only citizens of the United States who are citizens of this state are qualified to vote.'
measures.noMeans: Against Ratification: art. IV §1 keeps current wording ('Citizens of the state shall be entitled to vote'); statutory citizenship rule unchanged.

measures.title: People's Initiative to Limit Property Tax in Wyoming through a Homeowner's Property Exemption
measures.shortSummary: Exempts 50% of the assessed value of a qualified homeowner's primary residence from property tax for residents of one year who occupied it six months; first applicable tax year would be 2027.
measures.approvalRule: More than 50% of all ballots cast in the 2026 general election (not just votes on the measure) (Wyo. Const. art. 3 §52; SOS Initiative Process guide) Must receive FOR votes exceeding 50% of those voting in the general election; blank/undervotes on the proposition effectively count against it.
measures.yesMeans: 'FOR' enacts the 50% primary-residence homeowner's exemption.
measures.noMeans: 'AGAINST' leaves current property-tax exemptions unchanged.
